title: Gemini 4 Argon Built My Game AND Its Trailer… Then Microsoft Approved It
author: ExistentialHugger
selftext:
In this experiment, I used AI to create **Roving Rails**, an pixel-art train tycoon, and even generate a trailer for it.But here's the unexpected part: **the game was approved on the Microsoft Store the very same day.** From AI-generated code to a published game, this was a fun experiment in seeing how far AI-assisted game development can go.

🎮 Play Roving Rails: Train Tycoon on the Microsoft Store:  
[https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9MZ0DCZNRSTF](https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9MZ0DCZNRSTF)

I dont mean to be rude. I promise, i dont mean that. Its just that, argon was released almost...now..and u like made a game out of it in a couple of days. I dont get what the trailer is about, what i am buying and u also want $10. Its not even clear what is this game about.

replies.author: Valdaraak
replies.body:
> It's worth it

Nah. I can buy the Halo: Master Chief Collection for less. I could get Fallout 4 for half. I could toss a couple more bucks and get Dead Cells. Toss a buck extra and get Dying Light 2 - Reloaded Edition.

This game looks like $5, max. I'd be aiming more $2-$3 considering you probably spent less than a week making it.

replies.author: RedTheRobot
replies.body: You didn’t do any testing or quality control though. There are clearly defects in the game. While that is really no different than any AAA game nowadays it still gives AI development a bad name. Send a few hours and make sure your game has the polish it deserves, because if you won’t even play your game why would other?
